questions.text: If u = m cis(2π/3), write u³ in the form a + bi, in terms of m.
If (g + i)(2 + hi) = 6 – 2i, find all possible real values of g and h.
questions.markingGuide: LHS: (g + i)(2 + hi) = 2g + ghi + 2i + hi² = (2g – h) + (gh + 2)i. Equate real and imaginary parts with RHS 6 – 2i: 2g – h = 6 …(1) and gh + 2 = –2, so gh = –4 …(2). From (1): h = 2g – 6. Substitute into (2): g(2g – 6) = –4, i.e. 2g² – 6g + 4 = 0, so g² – 3g + 2 = 0. Factorise: (g – 1)(g – 2) = 0. So g = 1 giving h = 2(1) – 6 = –4, or g = 2 giving h = 2(2) – 6 = –2. Check (1 + i)(2 – 4i) = 2 – 4i + 2i – 4i² = 6 – 2i ✓ and (2 + i)(2 – 2i) = 4 – 4i + 2i – 2i² = 6 – 2i ✓.

questions.text: Expand and simplify (√(3a) – √(5a)i)², in terms of a.

questions.markingGuide: Expand LHS: (3 + 2√x)(1 + √x) = 3 + 3√x + 2√x + 2x = 3 + 5√x + 2x. Set equal to RHS: 3 + 5√x + 2x = 3 + 7√x, so 2x – 2√x = 0, i.e. 2√x(√x – 1) = 0. Therefore √x = 0 or √x = 1, giving x = 0 or x = 1. Check x = 1: LHS = (3 + 2)(1 + 1) = 10; RHS = 3 + 7 = 10 ✓. Check x = 0: LHS = 3·1 = 3; RHS = 3 ✓. Both valid.

questions.text: One solution of 2z³ + pz² + qz – 10 = 0 is z = 1 + 2i. If p, q are real, find the other solutions and p, q.
questions.expectedAnswer: p = –6, q = 14; other solutions z = 1–2i and z = 1
questions.markingGuide: z=1–2i also a root. Factor: z²–2z+5. f(z)=2(z²–2z+5)(z–a). Constant: 2(5)(–a)=–10. a=1. Expand: 2(z³–z²–2z²+2z+5z–5)=2(z³–3z²+7z–5)=2z³–6z²+14z–10. p=–6, q=14. Third root z=1.
